posts.text:
November is a good time for small-herd owners around Center and Shelby County to look at the hay already on hand before choosing supplemental feed.

Texas A&M AgriLife Extension recommends testing hay for protein and energy, then matching available hay and forage to cattle's needs. Age and stage matter: a cow nursing a calf has different needs from a dry cow. If adding concentrates or grain supplements, introduce them gradually rather than making a sudden change.

Which would help you most with that match—a hay test or sorting out the needs of different cattle? Either is a practical place to start.

AgriLife hay-testing guidance:
https://foragefax.tamu.edu/hay-testing-know-what-youre-feeding/

#ShelbyCountyTX #CenterTX #CattleCare

posts.text:
Planning your next garden in Center or Shelby County? Before choosing seeds or seedlings, a useful November project is finding out what your soil needs.

Texas A&M AgriLife says soil can be tested any time of year and recommends testing before buying or applying fertilizer. Results can help you understand nutrient levels and pH, so you can make decisions for your own garden instead of guessing.

Follow the testing lab's current sampling instructions, and keep the results with your garden notes. Then check the planting guidance for the particular crop you want to grow—not just a general “fall garden” list.

What are you hoping to grow next?

AgriLife soil-testing guidance:
https://agrilifetoday.tamu.edu/2025/03/27/boost-plant-growth-with-a-simple-soil-test/

#ShelbyCountyTX #EastTexasGardening #SoilTesting
posts.alt: November garden-preparation checklist: test soil before buying fertilizer, follow the testing lab's sampling instructions, and check planting dates for each crop.
